answers.question: A Moon base runs at 30% oxygen. What does NASA's testing actually cover?
answers.sentence: NASA's BASS-II tests cover 13.6–22.2% oxygen, so 30% oxygen is beyond what was tested — we can only show the closest tests, not an answer for that condition.
unknown: What happens at 30% oxygen — no BASS-II test goes above 22.2%
Airflow in cm/s (CSV has Fan display only; needs the fan calibration file)
Outcome (not in the PSI-25 CSV — only in the BASS-II report Appendix A)

answers.question: Do materials burn as well in microgravity as on Earth?
answers.sentence: At 21% oxygen the question is inside the tested range (13.6–22.2% oxygen, 129 BASS-II tests), but the honest answer is conditional: the tests cover microgravity burning across that oxygen range, and a direct burn-as-well-as-Earth comparison needs the airflow for each test, which is not in the sample yet.
unknown: Earth-control comparison — no Earth rows in the BASS-II sample
Airflow in cm/s (CSV has Fan display only; needs the fan calibration file)
Outcome (not in the PSI-25 CSV — only in the BASS-II report Appendix A)

answers.question: Compare two materials — PMMA film and SIBAL cloth. Which was tested at higher oxygen, and under what conditions?
answers.sentence: Both materials were tested inside the range: PMMA film test B1 at 22.2% oxygen is the highest-oxygen row in the sample, and SIBAL cloth test T25 at 20.8% oxygen is the closest SIBAL row — but which kept burning longer cannot be answered from the sample, because outcomes are not in the CSV.
unknown: Which material kept burning longer — outcomes are not in the PSI-25 CSV (BASS-II report Appendix A only)
